fields.title: Boundaries of what the model sees
fields.keyTakeaway: Context is assembled consciously for a budget, and silent truncation upon overflow is more dangerous than an error because the product keeps working incorrectly.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A long dialog starts "forgetting" the beginning. Why and what to do about it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The context window is a hard limit determining which product scenarios are possible. It also determines cost: the more we put in, the more expensive each call is. The decision on what to put in is a product decision.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[context-window|Context window]]** is the maximum context volume in tokens. In 2026, popular models range from tens of thousands to millions of tokens, and numbers continue to grow.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: What is important to understand besides size:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **A large window is not free.** We pay for all input tokens. A million tokens per query is expensive and slow, even if it fits technically.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Quality on long context drops.** The model finds information worse in the middle of a very long context than at the beginning or end. Putting everything in and hoping for the best is a bad strategy.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **What happens upon overflow.** Either an error or [[truncation|context truncation]]—part of it gets dropped. The second is more dangerous: the product works, but the model doesn't see what we thought it saw.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Hence the practice: **context is assembled consciously, not filled to the limit.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Three strategies when space runs short:
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: *Selection.* Put only what is relevant. This is RAG. *Compression.* Shorten: summarize dialog history, trim descriptions. *Sliding window.* Store the last N messages plus a brief summary of previous ones.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: For dialogs, usually a combination: last messages in full, earlier ones—compressed.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Recommendation chat assistant. Context budget—8 000 tokens, even though the window allows more. The limit was introduced for cost and speed.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The summary is updated every 6 messages via a separate cheap call. Costs 0.4 kopecks, saves orders of magnitude more.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: An incident that showed the danger of truncation: in the first version, upon overflow, the end of the prompt was cut off, which is where some of the found items ended up. The model answered "no such item exists" even though it was found. Diagnosed for a week because the error looked like a search problem.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: After this, upon budget overflow, the call is not made at all: context is trimmed at assembly stage, and truncation is logged.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Growing windows reduce the severity of the problem, but do not eliminate it: cost and quality degradation on long context remain.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Context is assembled consciously for a budget, and silent truncation upon overflow is more dangerous than an error because the product keeps working incorrectly.
